mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to tightened financing conditions.
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, no significant negative returns coincide with the trigger in non-stress regimes (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment) of at least 2,000 since the previous month's close is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as labor market strength supports corporate optimism.
failure_condition: In 20-day backtest, no statistically significant positive returns (t-test p > 0.05) when the trigger occurs during high-inflation periods.

mechanism_narrative: When the HOUST (residential construction) index exceeds 1,400 for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return is predicted to be positive, reflecting expectations of sustained economic expansion.
failure_condition: Over 5-year window, the 60-day forward return does not outperform a 5% risk-free rate benchmark during qualifying triggers.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 5% predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days due to contractionary supply dynamics.
failure_condition: In 100 triggers, less than 10% produce negative returns when not coincident with major external shocks.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return is expected to be positive due to improved labor market conditions and reduced risk aversion.
failure_condition: No significant positive returns in 20 out of 50 such regimes during non-crisis periods.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 3% and 5% respectively in the same month indicate strong dual demand, predicting a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > previous month GDPC1 + 3% AND RSAFS > previous month RSAFS + 5%
failure_condition: In 100 interaction triggers, less than 40 produce positive 20-day returns when inflation is above 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in CPIAUCSL (CPI) of at least 0.5% for two months suggests disinflation, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days as market expectations shift toward rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < previous month CPIAUCSL - 0.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 10 such triggers, no positive 60-day forward returns when the broader yield curve is flat.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (indicated by FEDFUNDS < 4.5% for 4 consecutive months), the S&P 500 is expected to deliver a positive 5-day forward return as liquidity conditions improve.
failure_condition: In 20 such regimes, less than 60% of 5-day forward returns are positive when equity volatility is elevated (>20% 30-day VIX).
